backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace train_y with its rank-transformed version before fitting (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n, or the equivalent ranks scaled to [0,1]). Fit the same RandomForestRegressor on the ranks and return its predictions unchanged. Since the metric is Spearman correlation, fitting ranks removes the influence of outlying clearance values on the splits.
backlog.title: Rank-transform the training target

backlog.spec: Clearance values are positive and right-skewed. Before fitting, replace train_y with np.log1p(np.clip(train_y, 0, None)) (or np.log10 with a small offset if values are all positive). Fit the existing random forest on the transformed target and return predictions in the transformed space; monotone transforms leave Spearman unchanged for the test ranking but change how the trees split.
backlog.title: Log-transform the target

backlog.spec: Extend featurize to concatenate the full RDKit descriptor set (Descriptors.descList, computed with calc on each Chem.MolFromSmiles result, replacing NaN and inf with 0 and clipping extreme values to the training 1st and 99th percentiles). Lipophilicity, polar surface area, H-bond counts and molecular weight are known drivers of hepatic clearance, so the random forest gets a compact, chemically meaningful feature block alongside the Morgan bits.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same Morgan generator, so each of the 2048 bits stores how many times an environment occurs instead of presence/absence. Keep radius 2 and the RandomForest unchanged. Counts carry more information about substructure multiplicity, which matters for size-related clearance trends.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with an atom invariant generator set to the feature-based invariants (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()), radius 2, 2048 bits. Feature invariants group atoms by pharmacophoric role (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) instead of element identity, which generalizes better across unseen scaffolds, the exact situation this grouped CV tests.
backlog.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP) fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add the 167-bit MACCS structural key fingerprint (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the feature matrix, concatenated to the Morgan bits. MACCS keys encode broad functional-group presence in a fixed, interpretable vocabulary and often help tree models on small ADME datasets where the Morgan space is sparse.
backlog.title: MACCS keys as features

backlog.spec: Compute RDKit atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, 2048 bits, counts) and topological torsion fingerprints (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, 1024 bits, counts) for each molecule. Concatenate them with the Morgan features before fitting the random forest. These encode longer-range topology than radius-2 Morgan environments and can capture molecular shape effects on enzymatic turnover.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological torsion fingerprints

backlog.spec: Keep the current features and model type, but sweep MAX_FEATURES over {'sqrt', 0.1, 0.3, 0.5} and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF over {1, 2, 3, 5} using an inner grouped validation on the training fold only (split the training molecules by Murcko scaffold, using the seed for the split). Pick the combination with the highest inner Spearman and refit on the whole training fold. Keeps the harness-visible interface unchanged.
backlog.title: Tune random forest max_features and leaf size

backlog.spec: Swap RandomForestRegressor for sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor with the same n_estimators, max_features and min_samples_leaf settings and random_state=seed. Extra trees use random split thresholds, which smooths the piecewise-constant predictions and often improves ranking performance on small noisy datasets.
backlog.title: Replace random forest with extra trees

backlog.spec: Replace the random forest with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor on the same Morgan bits. Use n_estimators around 400, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.5, reg_lambda 1.0, and random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Boosting often beats bagged trees on tabular fingerprint data, though it needs the stronger regularization given here.
backlog.title: Gradient boosting with LightGBM

backlog.spec: Train catboost.CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, 800 iterations, loss RMSE, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on the Morgan bits plus the RDKit descriptor block. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees are robust to overfitting on a few hundred to a thousand molecules, which suits this small set.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor on fingerprints and descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute Morgan bit vectors (radius 2, 2048 bits). Build a Tanimoto (Jaccard) kernel matrix K(a,b)=sum(min)/sum(max) on counts or bits between training molecules and between test and training molecules. Fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge with kernel='precomputed' and alpha around 0.5 (center train_y by its mean and add the mean back to predictions). Similarity-based kernels suit scaffold-split generalization better than trees in many ADME benchmarks.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge with Tanimoto similarity

backlog.spec: Use the same precomputed Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bits as in the kernel ridge idea, but fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, epsilon=0.05). Predictions are the decision values on the test-by-train kernel. SVR's epsilon-insensitive loss is robust to the noisy tail of clearance measurements.
backlog.title: Support vector regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Compute a Tanimoto kernel matrix on Morgan bit vectors for train and train-by-test pairs. Fit a GP via sklearn.gaussian_process.GaussianProcessRegressor with kernel = ConstantKernel times a precomputed-equivalent Tanimoto (implement by fitting the noise-regularized posterior mean manually: alpha_hat = (K + sigma^2 I)^-1 (y - mean), with sigma^2 chosen from {0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by inner grouped CV on the training fold). Return the posterior mean at test points, which gives calibrated similarity-weighted predictions.
backlog.title: Gaussian process regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: For each test molecule, find the k nearest training molecules under Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bits (k around 7). Predict the similarity-weighted mean of their train_y values (weights = similarity to the power 3). Fall back to the global training mean if all similarities are zero. This is a simple, interpretable baseline that is often competitive with forests on scaffold-held-out sets.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbour Tanimoto regression

backlog.spec: Compute predictions from the existing random forest on Morgan bits and from a Tanimoto-kernel ridge regressor on the same features. Convert both prediction vectors to ranks within the test set and average them with equal weight, returning the averaged rank score. Blending models with different inductive biases usually improves Spearman more than tuning either alone.
backlog.title: Ensemble of random forest and kernel model

backlog.spec: Train three random forests with different inputs (Morgan bits; RDKit descriptors; MACCS keys) using seeds seed, seed+1, seed+2. Average their predictions on the test molecules (equal weights). Each view captures different chemistry, and averaging decorrelates the errors.
backlog.title: Ensemble of tree models with different feature sets

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold grouped (Murcko scaffold) inner split on the training molecules to produce out-of-fold predictions from three base learners: random forest on Morgan bits, LightGBM on descriptors, and Tanimoto kernel ridge. Fit a non-negative linear regression on the stacked OOF predictions to find blend weights, then refit each base learner on all training molecules and combine the test predictions with those weights.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble with out-of-fold weights

backlog.spec: Train 10 random forests, each on a bootstrap resample of the training molecules drawn with a seed-derived RNG and each with fewer trees (about 60), then average their predictions. The averaged result is a bag of bags with extra variance reduction, which can reduce the sensitivity of the ranking to the particular training fold.
backlog.title: Bagged ensemble over bootstrap resamples

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and weight each sample in the random forest fit by 1 divided by the count of molecules sharing its scaffold (sample_weight argument of fit, normalized to mean 1). This stops heavily represented scaffold series from dominating the splits, which better matches the test condition of unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware sample weighting

backlog.spec: Before fitting, group training molecules that have identical canonical SMILES (after RDKit canonicalization with isomericSmiles=False) and replace their train_y with the group mean. Then fit the existing random forest on the deduplicated set. Duplicate or near-identical entries add noisy repeated samples that distort the forest's leaf values.
backlog.title: Scaffold-based duplicate handling and target averaging

backlog.spec: Clip train_y to the 2nd and 98th percentiles of the training fold before fitting, then fit the existing random forest. Winsorizing removes extreme measurement values that can pull leaf averages and degrade the ranking of the bulk of compounds, while leaving the rank order of test predictions basically intact.
backlog.title: Outlier clipping of the target

backlog.spec: Using LightGBM on Morgan bits plus descriptors, run a small random search (8 configurations) over num_leaves {7,15,31}, learning_rate {0.02,0.05}, n_estimators {200,500}, min_child_samples {5,10,20}, and colsample_bytree {0.3,0.6}. Score each configuration with a 4-fold inner Murcko-grouped split of the training fold using Spearman, keep the best, refit on all training data. Keep the total runtime well under the job limit by using n_jobs=8.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter tuning of LightGBM via inner grouped CV

backlog.spec: Train lightgbm.LGBMRanker with objective 'lambdarank' (or rank_xendcg) on Morgan bits plus descriptors, treating the whole training fold as one query group. Convert train_y to integer relevance labels by binning into 10 quantile levels. Predict scores on the test set. Directly optimizing ranking pairs targets the Spearman metric better than squared error.
backlog.title: Ranking objective with LightGBM lambdarank

backlog.spec: Train a small multilayer perceptron in sklearn (MLPRegressor, hidden layers (256,128), alpha=1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.15, random_state=seed, max_iter 500) on standardized RDKit descriptors plus Morgan counts. Standardize inputs using training-fold statistics only, and standardize train_y. The MLP gives smooth nonlinear predictions that complement tree models in an ensemble.
backlog.title: Pairwise ranking loss with a neural MLP

backlog.spec: On the training fold only, drop Morgan bits that are set in fewer than 2 or more than 98 percent of molecules, and drop one of each pair of bits with absolute Pearson correlation above 0.95. Then fit the existing random forest on the reduced feature matrix. Removing redundant and near-constant bits reduces noise in the random subsampling of features at each split.
backlog.title: Feature selection by variance and correlation before forest

backlog.spec: Fit a preliminary random forest (100 trees) on the training fold, keep the top 512 features by impurity-based importance, then fit the final random forest (N_TREES trees) on only those features for the test predictions. Selecting informative features within each fold, not globally, avoids leaking test information and cuts noise dimensions.
backlog.title: Feature selection by random forest importance

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit the existing random forest with three different internal random states derived from seed (seed, seed+1000, seed+2000) and average their test predictions. This reduces Monte Carlo variance in the ranking, which matters since the noise sd of the job score is already about 0.007.
backlog.title: Multiple seeds averaged for the final prediction

backlog.spec: Split train_y into 5 quantile bins and fit sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier on the bin labels with the existing features and settings. For each test molecule, predict the expected bin index from predict_proba (sum of bin index times probability) and return it as the score. Classification into ordinal bins gives a smoother ranking signal than regression on noisy values.
backlog.title: Quantile-based target discretization for classification forest

backlog.spec: Build two base predictors: a LightGBM regressor on RDKit descriptors only and an extra-trees regressor on Morgan counts. Convert each prediction set to its within-test-set rank, then average the ranks with weights 0.6 and 0.4 and return the blended score. Mixing descriptor-based and fingerprint-based views yields diverse errors that help the rank correlation on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Mixed ensemble of trees and kernel model with rank averaging on descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute RDKit Crippen logP (Descriptors.MolLogP), TPSA and molecular weight for each molecule, cached by SMILES like _DESC_CACHE. Build a third score as the rank-average of MolLogP (sign +1) and TPSA (sign -1) on the test set, since hepatocyte clearance tends to rise with lipophilicity and fall with polarity. Final output = (0.5 * current blend rank + 0.5 * ... ) is replaced by a weighted sum: 0.8 * current blend rank + 0.2 * prior rank. Keep the weight fixed at 0.2; do not tune it on the test folds. No new model is fitted, so runtime is unchanged.
backlog.title: Crippen logP and TPSA as a rank-blended lipophilicity prior

backlog.spec: In the descriptor LightGBM, pass monotone_constraints so that the features MolLogP and TPSA are constrained to increase and decrease respectively, and set the other entries to 0. Look up column indices from the Descriptors.descList names (for example 'MolLogP' and 'TPSA'). Keep all other hyperparameters as they are. The idea is to stop the trees from learning non-monotone noise along the two most physically plausible axes of clearance, which should regularise the model on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on LightGBM for physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: For each molecule, embed one conformer with rdkit.Chem.AllChem.EmbedMolecule (using ETKDGv3 with randomSeed=seed or a fixed 42, and a fallback to a 2D-only zero vector if embedding fails), then compute the principal moments of inertia ratios (rdMolDescriptors.CalcNPR1, CalcNPR2), CalcPMI1-3, radius of gyration, asphericity, spherocity and CalcNumAmideBonds. Append these to desc_features for the LightGBM model. Cache results by SMILES so each molecule is embedded only once across the 15 fits. Wrap embedding in a try/except and keep runtime below the 10-minute limit by using a single conformer.
backlog.title: 3D conformer shape descriptors from ETKDG embeddings

backlog.spec: Add a third model: a feed-forward neural network from sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor with hidden layers (256, 64), ReLU, alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True with a 10% validation split, and max_iter=500. Its inputs are the descriptor matrix after sklearn.preprocessing.QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') fitted on the training fold, concatenated with the Morgan count vector scaled by log1p. Average 5 networks trained with seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4. Rank-average its test predictions with the existing two models using equal weights of 1/3 each.
backlog.title: Small MLP on quantile-transformed descriptors and fingerprints

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first run the current blend on test_smiles to get rank scores in [0,1]. Keep the 50% of test molecules whose two model predictions agree most closely (smallest absolute difference between the LightGBM rank and the ExtraTrees rank). Append those molecules to the training set with pseudo-targets equal to their blended rank score, then refit both models on the augmented set and produce the final blend. Use only the seed argument for randomness. This uses unlabelled test structures, which is allowed because the harness passes test_smiles and no labels; it should help the model adapt to the unseen scaffolds in each fold.
backlog.title: Transductive pseudo-labelling of the test molecules

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) of each training molecule. Draw 8 bootstrap bags by sampling scaffold groups with replacement (keeping all molecules in each sampled scaffold), so each bag mimics the unseen-scaffold split used by the harness. Fit the LightGBM and ExtraTrees pair on each bag with seed+bag_index, predict test_smiles, and average the rank scores of the bags within each model before the 0.6/0.4 blend. Reduce ExtraTrees to 200 trees per bag to stay within the 10-minute limit.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped bagging of the whole ensemble

backlog.spec: In the descriptor LightGBM, replace the fixed learning_rate=0.03 with a cosine schedule from 0.05 down to 0.005 across the 400 rounds. Implement it with lgb.train (or LGBMRegressor.fit callbacks) using a callback that calls env.model.reset_parameter({'learning_rate': lr_t}) at each iteration, where lr_t = 0.005 + 0.5*(0.05-0.005)*(1+cos(pi*t/400)). Keep all other parameters the same. The goal is to take larger steps early and fine adjustments late, which may reduce overfitting to the training scaffolds without adding trees.
backlog.title: Cosine learning-rate decay over boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Keep the rank-transformed target y = rankdata(train_y)/n. Change the descriptor LightGBM objective from the default L2 to 'huber' with alpha=0.2, which is the scale of the rank target. Keep the ExtraTrees model and the blend unchanged. Huber loss limits the influence of the extreme-rank molecules, which are often assay outliers in the public clearance data, while still fitting the central ordering that Spearman rewards.
backlog.title: Huber objective on the rank-transformed target

backlog.spec: Before fitting, compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix between training molecules from their binary Morgan (radius 2, 2048 bits) fingerprints, using numpy dot products on the bit matrix. For each training molecule, keep its top 5 neighbours by similarity (excluding itself) with similarity above 0.4, and replace its rank target with a weighted mean of its own rank (weight 0.5) and the neighbours' ranks (weights proportional to similarity, total 0.5). If a molecule has no neighbour above 0.4, keep its rank unchanged. Fit both models on the smoothed targets. This is a label-denoising step that uses only training labels and is fully determined by the seed-free inputs.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-neighbour smoothing of training targets

backlog.spec: Switch the descriptor LightGBM to boosting_type='dart' with drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, and max_drop=50, keeping n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, and the other parameters. DART randomly drops previously built trees during training, which regularises the ensemble much as dropout does in neural networks and can reduce variance on small datasets like this one. Use random_state=seed. Keep the ExtraTrees model and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: DART boosting for the descriptor model

backlog.spec: Replace the single Morgan-bit Tanimoto kernel in the GP with a weighted sum of normalized Tanimoto kernels computed on four binary fingerprints: Morgan radius 2 (2048 bits), atom-pair (2048 bits), topological torsion (2048 bits) and MACCS keys (166 bits). Compute each K_i = tanimoto(X_i, X_i) on the training set and the matching train-test block. Choose the noise sigma2 from (0.1, 0.3, 1.0) and kernel weights from a small grid (each weight in {0, 0.5, 1}, not all zero) by the existing GroupKFold-by-scaffold Spearman search on the training data. Keep gp_mean unchanged and use the combined kernel K = sum_i w_i K_i in both the fit and the prediction. Keep the rest of fit_predict, including the descriptor LightGBM rank blend.
backlog.title: Multiple-kernel Tanimoto GP over several fingerprints

backlog.spec: Turn the fingerprint GP into a residual model. Inside fit_predict, first compute out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training molecules using GroupKFold(5) with Murcko scaffold groups, so the residuals are honest. Set r = y - oof, where y is the rank-transformed target. Fit the Tanimoto-kernel GP (existing gp_mean and choose_sigma2 applied to r, with the same sigma2 grid) and predict residuals for the test molecules. The fingerprint-side prediction is the full LightGBM test prediction (trained on all training data) plus the GP residual prediction. Rank-blend this combined score with the existing LightGBM rank at weight 0.5 each, and keep seed handling unchanged.
backlog.title: Residual GP on top of descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add a second fingerprint family for the Tanimoto GP: RDKit Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints (rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory with Generate.Gen2DFingerprint), folded to a fixed-length binary vector of about 2048 bits with the same bit-folding method for train and test. Build the training Tanimoto kernel and the test-train block from these bits, and use it in place of the Morgan kernel inside the existing choose_sigma2 and gp_mean. Keep the descriptor LightGBM model and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend. Cache fingerprint computation per SMILES as the descriptor code does, to stay well under the 10-minute job limit.
backlog.title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints as a GP kernel

backlog.spec: Instead of using only the final LightGBM model, train the descriptor LightGBM once with n_estimators=400 and learning_rate=0.03 as now, then predict the test set at several checkpoints with lgbm.predict(X, num_iteration=k) for k in {100, 200, 300, 400}. Average the four predictions after ranking each, and use that averaged rank as the descriptor score in the existing 0.6/0.4 blend. This gives a cheap, smooth stopping-time ensemble with no extra training cost. Keep all other parts of fit_predict unchanged.
backlog.title: Snapshot ensemble over LightGBM boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Add a standardization step applied to every SMILES before any featurization (desc_features, bit_fingerprints, and the scaffold computation in choose_sigma2). Parse each SMILES, keep the largest covalently bonded fragment (sort fragments by heavy-atom count and keep the largest), neutralize formal charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and re-canonicalize with Chem.MolToSmiles. Fall back to the original SMILES if parsing fails. Use the standardized strings consistently for all train and test features and for the Murcko scaffold groups. Leave the rest of the model unchanged.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules before featurization

backlog.spec: After computing the blended test scores, refine them by label-propagation-style smoothing over the test set. Compute the Tanimoto matrix among test molecules from the Morgan bits. For each test molecule, average its own blended rank score with the scores of its k=5 most similar other test molecules, weighted by Tanimoto similarity, with a mixing weight alpha=0.3 on the neighbour average. Re-rank the final output to [0,1]. Only test-side information is used, so no test labels are involved. Keep the training pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Transductive smoothing of test predictions over the test-test similarity graph

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 0.6/0.4 rank blend with a weight search. Use three rank-normalized components: the descriptor LightGBM prediction, the Tanimoto GP prediction, and an equal-weight average of the two. Inside fit_predict, compute out-of-fold predictions of the two base models on the training data with GroupKFold(5) over Murcko scaffolds, then grid-search blend weights on the simplex with step 0.1 to maximize Spearman against the rank-transformed training target. Apply the chosen weights to the test-set ranks of the full-data models. Keep the seed argument for LightGBM and the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Blend weights chosen by inner grouped CV over three model ranks

backlog.spec: Replace the global Tanimoto GP prediction with a local one. For each test molecule, select the k=150 training molecules with highest Tanimoto similarity to it, then solve the GP mean formula (gp_mean with the chosen sigma2) using only that neighbour set, with the Tanimoto kernel restricted to those molecules. Process test molecules in batches of 64 to bound memory, and use the same sigma2 chosen by choose_sigma2 on the full training set. This gives a locally adaptive kernel model. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Local GP on the k most similar training molecules

backlog.spec: Adjust the descriptor LightGBM toward stronger regularization. Set extra_trees=True, reg_lambda=5.0, min_child_samples=20, colsample_bytree=0.3 and add feature_fraction_bynode=0.5, while keeping n_estimators=600 and learning_rate=0.02. Keep subsample=0.8 and subsample_freq=1 and the rank-transformed target. Everything else in fit_predict stays unchanged, including the GP fingerprint model and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend.
backlog.title: Regularized LightGBM with extra-trees splits and node-level feature sampling

backlog.spec: Add a kernel-approximation model on the descriptors. Clip the descriptor matrix, standardize it with statistics from the training fold, then clip each standardized column to [-5, 5]. Build 1000 random Fourier features for an RBF kernel with bandwidth set to the median pairwise distance of the training set and the seed controlling the random frequencies. Fit ridge regression with alpha=1.0 on the rank-transformed target and predict the test set. Rank-average this prediction with the existing descriptor LightGBM and GP predictions in equal thirds. The seed argument controls the random frequencies.
backlog.title: Random Fourier features on descriptors with ridge regression as a smooth second model

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, remove the GroupKFold search in choose_sigma2. Instead choose the GP noise sigma2 by maximizing the GP log marginal likelihood on the full training kernel K_tr. Use scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar over log(sigma2) in [log 0.02, log 3]. The objective is 0.5*y'alpha + sum(log diag(L)) with L = cholesky(K + sigma2*I) and y centred by its mean. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Type-II maximum-likelihood GP noise

backlog.spec: Replace the Tanimoto kernel in the GP with K_p = K ** p, where p is chosen from {1, 2, 3} jointly with sigma2 by the existing inner grouped CV loop in choose_sigma2, using the same Spearman criterion. Powering a similarity in [0,1] emphasises close neighbours and suppresses weak similarity, which may help on scaffold-disjoint folds. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Sharpened Tanimoto kernel via power

backlog.spec: Build a second kernel from the RDKit descriptor matrix. Standardize desc_features with training-set mean and std, clip to [-5, 5], and compute an RBF kernel exp(-||x-x'||^2 / (2*d)), where d is the number of descriptors. Use the elementwise product K_tanimoto * K_rbf as the GP kernel and choose sigma2 with the existing grouped CV loop. A molecule then counts as similar only when both its substructure fingerprint and its physchem profile agree. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Product kernel of Tanimoto and RBF on descriptors

backlog.spec: Give each training molecule its own noise variance in the GP. For each training molecule compute its local density as the mean Tanimoto similarity to its 5 nearest training neighbours. Set noise_i = sigma2 * (1 + c / (density_i + 0.05)) with c = 0.5, so sparse molecules are regularised more. Solve (K + diag(noise)) alpha = y - mean as before, and keep sigma2 chosen by the existing CV loop. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Density-dependent heteroscedastic GP noise

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan bit Tanimoto kernel with a Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree kernel on the molecular graph. Start with atom labels from atomic number, degree, formal charge, and aromaticity. Run 3 WL refinement iterations, where each atom's label is a hash of its own label and the sorted labels of its neighbours. Count label occurrences per molecule over all iterations to get a sparse count vector, normalise each vector to unit L2 norm, and use the dot product as the kernel. Keep sigma2 chosen by the existing CV loop and the descriptor LightGBM blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree kernel for the GP

backlog.spec: Build an ensemble of 10 GP members. Each member uses a random 50% subset of the 2048 Morgan bits, drawn with a seed-derived RandomState, and computes its own Tanimoto kernel and CV-chosen sigma2. Average the member predictions on the test set before the rank blend with the descriptor LightGBM. Each member sees only part of the substructure space, so the average is less dependent on any single bit family.
backlog.title: Random-subspace GP ensemble over fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Fit the descriptor LightGBM as before. Use its leaf indices (lgbm.predict(X, pred_leaf=True)) as a categorical fingerprint: one-hot encode each (tree, leaf) pair into a sparse binary vector. Define a Tanimoto-style kernel on these vectors using the same formula as tanimoto(), and fit the GP mean on it with sigma2 chosen by the existing CV loop. The resulting kernel measures how often two molecules fall into the same leaves, which is a learned similarity. Blend its rank with the Morgan GP and the LightGBM rank using equal weights.
backlog.title: Tree-leaf embedding kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the single descriptor LightGBM fit with three cosine-restart cycles. Each cycle trains 150 trees, starting with learning_rate 0.05 and decaying to 0.005 within the cycle, and each cycle continues from the previous one with init_model. Take the test prediction at the end of each cycle, rank-average the three snapshots, and use this as the descriptor score in the existing blend. Keep the GP and the blend weight unchanged.
backlog.title: Cyclic-restart LightGBM with rank snapshots

backlog.spec: Append to the descriptor matrix a block of ring-system features. For each molecule, take Murcko scaffold ring systems via MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol and count ring systems by size, number of rings in each system, and the number of distinct scaffold types seen in training as a frequency-encoded value. Use a fixed-width vector of 12 values, concatenated to desc_features before the LightGBM fit. Keep the GP and the blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Ring-system and scaffold count features

backlog.spec: Before the descriptor LightGBM fit, augment the training set with 2000 synthetic rows. Each synthetic row is a convex combination lambda*x_i + (1-lambda)*x_j of two standardized descriptor rows with lambda ~ Beta(0.4, 0.4) and the same mix of their rank targets. Concatenate these rows with the originals (seed-controlled RandomState) and fit LightGBM as before. Mixup smooths the descriptor surface between molecules and may reduce overfitting to individual scaffolds. Keep the GP and the blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation on descriptor features

backlog.spec: In desc_features, append a small block of counts computed with RDKit SMARTS patterns (Chem.MolFromSmarts, matched with GetSubstructMatches, counted per molecule, cached alongside the descriptor list). Use about 12 patterns: carboxylic acid, tetrazole, aliphatic primary/secondary/tertiary amine, quaternary N, aromatic N-heterocycle, phenol, O-methyl or N-methyl, benzylic CH2/CH3, ester, amide, sulfonamide, and aromatic halogen. These flags capture ionization state and labile metabolic sites that drive hepatocyte clearance. Keep everything else unchanged, including the rank target, the LightGBM settings and the GP blend.
backlog.title: Ionization and metabolic soft-spot SMARTS counts as descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the target line y = rankdata(train_y)/len(train_y) with normal scores: y = scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(train_y) - 0.5) / len(train_y)). Ranks are unchanged, so the Spearman ordering of the training labels is preserved, but the spacing of the regression target becomes Gaussian. Both the LightGBM fit and the GP mean are then fit on this target, and the final blend still uses rankdata on the predictions. This is a single-line change.
backlog.title: Gaussian-rank (normal-score) target transform

backlog.spec: Add a third model to fit_predict: a sklearn ElasticNetCV (l1_ratio in [0.2, 0.5, 0.8], 5 inner folds, max_iter 5000) on standardized, quantile-clipped descriptor features (fit the StandardScaler on training data only, clip to the training 1st and 99th percentiles). Its test predictions are rank-normalized and blended with the existing LightGBM and GP ranks using weights 0.4, 0.4, 0.2. Linear models are a different inductive bias from trees and kernels, so they may add diversity cheaply.
backlog.title: Linear ElasticNet on standardized descriptors as a third blend member

backlog.spec: In gp_mean, replace the constant prior mean mu = y.mean() with a local prior: for each test molecule, use the mean target of its k=10 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules (computed from the same K matrices). For the GP fit, the training prior is the leave-self-out kNN mean within the training set. Keep the GP posterior as a residual correction: pred = prior + K_te @ alpha, where alpha solves (K_tr + sigma2 I) alpha = y - prior_tr. Keep sigma2 selection by grouped CV as it is now.
backlog.title: Gaussian process with a kNN-based prior mean

backlog.spec: Cluster the training molecules into k=4 groups with sklearn KMeans (n_init=5, random_state=seed) on a 64-component TruncatedSVD of the Morgan bit matrix. Fit a separate Tanimoto-kernel GP (with the same sigma2 selection) on each cluster. At prediction time, route each test molecule by its nearest cluster centroid and use that cluster's GP. Blend this routed prediction with the global GP at 50/50 before the rank blend with descriptor LightGBM. This adds locality in chemical space that a single global GP cannot capture.
backlog.title: Mixture of local GPs over k-means clusters of the fingerprint space

backlog.spec: Before the final fits, compute leave-one-out predictions of the Tanimoto GP on the training set using the closed-form LOO residual of kernel ridge: r_i = alpha_i / (Ginv)_ii, where Ginv = (K + sigma2 I)^-1 and alpha = Ginv y. Drop the 5% of training molecules with the largest absolute LOO residual (only from the GP and LightGBM fits, not from the sigma2 search). Use the same kept subset for both models. This removes likely label noise from the training data without changing the test set.
backlog.title: Leave-one-out residual pruning of noisy training labels

backlog.spec: Build the fingerprint with a custom atom invariant instead of the default. Use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with an atomInvariantsGenerator (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganAtomInvariants or a custom list) so that each atom's initial identity includes formal charge, aromaticity, total H count, and ring membership in addition to element and degree. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits, and keep the Tanimoto GP unchanged. The goal is to make the GP distinguish ionized and ring-embedded atoms, which the default invariant conflates.
backlog.title: Alternative atom invariants for Morgan features

backlog.spec: Replace the single choose_sigma2 pick with a bagged average. Compute the grouped-CV Spearman score for each sigma2 in (0.1, 0.3, 1.0), then convert those scores to softmax weights with temperature 0.02 and form the GP prediction as the weighted average of the three gp_mean posteriors on the test set (the training kernel is reused, so this costs little). This hedges the noise-level choice when the grouped-CV scores are close, which they often are at noise sd 0.007.
backlog.title: Ensemble of GP posteriors over a sigma2 grid instead of one selected value

backlog.spec: Make the GP noise term per-sample. Start with weights w_i = 1 and sigma2_i = sigma2 / w_i. Solve (K + diag(sigma2_i)) alpha = y - mu, compute the residuals r_i = y_i minus the training fitted value, and set w_i = min(1, c / |r_i|) with c = 1.345 times the median absolute residual. Iterate three times. Predictions use the final alpha. This down-weights training molecules whose labels disagree with their Tanimoto neighbours, using a Huber rule, and leaves the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Huber-robust GP via iteratively reweighted noise

backlog.spec: Replace the single fingerprint with a choice among three configurations: radius 1 with 1024 bits, radius 2 with 2048 bits (current), and radius 3 with 4096 bits. Pick the configuration by the same grouped 5-fold Spearman criterion already used for sigma2, jointly over the (configuration, sigma2) pairs, inside fit_predict on training data only. Use the chosen configuration for the test predictions. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged. The selection stays within training data, so no test leakage occurs.
backlog.title: Morgan radius and bit-size sweep for the Tanimoto GP

incumbent.description: Replace the fingerprint ExtraTrees with a Tanimoto-kernel GP posterior mean on Morgan bit vectors, choosing the noise sigma^2 from {0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by inner scaffold-grouped CV on the training fold.

memo: Helped: moving from the RF baseline (about 0.6103) to a rank-averaged blend of descriptor LightGBM plus a fingerprint model (0.5337), then rank-transforming the target (0.5123), then swapping ExtraTrees for a Tanimoto-kernel GP on Morgan bits (0.4971/0.4965; incumbent, mean_adjusted 0.4968 over 2 runs). Did not help: sample weighting, bit filtering, feature selection, LightGBM or CatBoost swaps, stacking, monotone constraints, count or FCFP kernels, multi-kernel sums, MACCS bits, target smoothing, blend-weight search (+0.0060), lipophilicity prior, and LightGBM regularization or tuning. MLP, SVR, kernel ridge and random Fourier features looked good on first runs (0.4879-0.4943) but their replicates were worse. Noise sd is about 0.0070, so gains under that are unreliable. Most of the 40-slot budget has been spent, with 6 aborts from not reading the file first. Next: read the current file first, tune GP noise and Morgan radius/size, and try a replicated MLP or RFF ensemble for diversity.
